title: Lifetime Extension — and Where It Fails
prompt: Returning a reference to a temporary can never be safe, so `extended()` must back its reference with *static* storage. And `holderTrap()` returns the value a correct `Holder` would have captured **by value** instead of by reference.

tests.name: extended stays valid
tests.hint: Only static/dynamic storage survives; return a reference to a function-local static string containing "static".

tests.name: holderTrap returns the salvageable value
tests.hint: Copy the temporary into a return value — return std::string("salvaged ..."); — that is what a correct Holder does with a value member instead of a reference.
